findings.reason: §5 and §10 are both `done` and f-wil-001 already orders "§11 after §7", so the omission changes no dispatch and only leaves the record short of its own convention.
findings.text: `s11` records a dependency on §7 alone, while §11's write scope overlaps §5 (`imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py`) and §10 (`imas_ambix/agent/index_placement.py`) and its items 1 and 3 modify a predicate and a rollup column those sections introduced; the plan's own convention declares such overlaps (`s5:[s3]` for the shared `telemetry_index.py`, `s10:[s6]` for the shared `cli.py`), so the declared dependency set is incomplete

findings.reason: a node implementing item 5 as written adds whole-hour coverage that still passes under the regression, whereas the declared negative control only becomes reachable once the day-period assertion is made independent of the raw reference, so the stated cause misdirects the repair the section asks for.
findings.text: §11 item 5 states "the counter-rollup test never forces whole hours through `hourly_rollup`", but the test it cites, `test_cached_tiers_*` (tests/test_agent_telemetry_watch.py:481-513), queries a one-day period, selects exactly the whole-hour rows (`SELECT counter_diff, segments FROM hourly_rollup WHERE name_id = ... AND hour > ? AND hour < ?`, tests/test_agent_telemetry_watch.py:504-510) and asserts those rows exist, so whole hours are already read from the rollup; the real reason a raw-answering regression passes is that the assertion is `observed == reference` against the `_RawIndex` arm, whose `_counter_window_rows` computes from raw rows (tests/test_agent_telemetry_watch.py:36-52, 498-501)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every anchor §11 names resolves in the tree as read: `index_placement.index_requires_rebuild` (imas_ambix/agent/index_placement.py:95), its own `name_id` copy (index_placement.py:98), `cli.py`'s private `_snapshot_paths` call (imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:3420), the inline `-wal`/`-shm` clearing (imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:3431-3435), `restore_index`'s install by `os.replace` (imas_ambix/agent/index_placement.py:264), and the counter rollup's `counter_diff` column (imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:320) with `_counter_window_rows` reading `segments` (imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:2126).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §11's done-whens are each measurable (`git grep name_id -- imas_ambix/agent/index_placement.py`, `git grep _snapshot_paths -- imas_ambix/agent/cli.py`, `os.replace` confined to `index_placement` plus its stale-`-wal` regression) and the section declares a negative control whose refusal is observable in a test's exit status.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §11 names no scratchpad or node-local path; its gates are the named test modules and the whole-tree ruff run, executed on the fleet allocation and logged where the plan's other sections log.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §11's symbols and prose name mechanisms (`name_id`, `_snapshot_paths`, `segments`, `-wal`) and carry no plan label, ticket number or version tag into code; the `§5`/`§10` references are plan prose, not code or comments.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — item 5's stated reason for the counter-rollup test's blindness is contradicted by the test it cites.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §11 carries one verdict for one cleanup: each of its five items makes one index fact or one install path single-owned, and none of them is a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — `s11` declares `depends-on` only `watch-index-lifecycle#s7`, although §11 also edits `imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py` (§5's file) and `imas_ambix/agent/index_placement.py` (§10's file), whose code its items 1 and 3 change.
